correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed both base- and line-graph updates. On the line graph a resting edge is excited precisely if an endpoint is incident to an excited edge; encoding excited and refractory bit planes yielded a fresh successor array. Iterating the image of the entire state set to a stable image isolates the cycle states, since the stable image is permuted by the update, and every cycle survives. Reverse substitution through deleted layers recovers exact first-entry distances. The replay covered all 14,348,907 configurations per line graph, matched all 46 and 37 nonzero period/entry cells and all 186 and 150 exceptional temporal representatives after phase canonicalization, and independently confirmed the base counts. Maximal entry depths are 17 (80 states) and 12 (1,200 states), all eventual period three. Exhaustive base permutations of orders 20 and 120 give the reported orbit-size partitions. The line graph recovers each base vertex as a triangle because both base graphs are cubic and triangle-free, so those permutations give the full spatial group. The repaired comparison and references do not alter any dynamics or numerical claim.
residual_risks: Exact computational classification of specified finite maps; not a formal proof assistant certificate, and not evidence of a general preservation theorem.
